problem: Existing evaluations of MLLM agents either use game worlds, bounded indoor scenes, or street-view/aerial imagery hopping between sampled viewpoints, or generated urban simulators; none preserve a real, georegistered metropolis with continuous collision-constrained motion, so it is unknown whether local perception composes into sustained action at city scale.
motivation: Reliable urban action depends on whether local evidence stays useful after the agent moves, turns a corner and the landmark leaves view. Strong single-view recognition does not show that a spatial estimate survives continued closed-loop action, so a benchmark must expose the transition from local grounding to long-horizon navigation and adaptation under one geographic frame.
key_idea: Build a Unity sandbox from Hong Kong's territory-wide 3D Visualisation Map and 3D Pedestrian Network, and evaluate MLLM agents on a five-level ladder (local QA, navigation, implicit-goal search, multi-task planning, dynamic changes) with a fixed first-person + map interface.
insight: MLLMs have decent atomic skills (visual recognition up to 93.8%) but orientation is near chance for several models (23.3-58.3% vs 25% random), and success collapses from short navigation to long navigation (best 5.0%). The oracle-checkpoint analysis shows GPT-5.5 gets closer than start in 98.8% of LongNav episodes when the best checkpoint is used, versus 57.5% observed, so progress is made and then lost, and agents do not correct errors. High pedestrian-network adherence (about 93-98%) alongside low closure compliance (10-46.7%) and high pedestrian collision rates shows that locally plausible motion does not mean adaptation.
method: Geospatial layer: loads the Hong Kong Lands Department Cesium 3D Tiles mesh (WGS84) into Unity at runtime and streams it by view scale. The mesh gives rendering and collision geometry, and the 3D Pedestrian Network is imported as a georeferenced graph in the same frame.

Simulation layer: continuous first-person character motion with collision. Adds time-of-day (day/dusk/night), weather (rain, fog, cloudy), and Rocketbox animated pedestrians on the network. Logs pose, collisions, rain exposure, and pedestrian contact each step.

Agent layer: client-server interface to an external MLLM, with the simulator paused while it awaits a response. Observation is first-person RGB plus text history and an interactive map with no route shown. Actions are move/sprint/look/jump/open_map, map_select/pan/zoom/orbit/close_map, and terminate, in a JSON ReAct format.

Five-level evaluation ladder: L1 local understanding (visual recognition, orientation, active exploration QA); L2 explicit navigation (short, long, instructional, constrained); L3 implicit (place search, intent inference); L4 multi-task (time-window, multi-stop); L5 dynamic (road closure replanning, navigation among pedestrians).

Human-verified benchmark: 810 base instances across Hong Kong, each completed by annotators within the 150-step limit and double-checked. Metrics are answer accuracy, success within 15 m, pedestrian-network adherence (PNA), closure compliance rate (CCR), and pedestrian-collision rate (PCR).
Diagnostic analyses: distance-stratified success bins, closer-than-start and multi-stop partial progress, GPT-5.5 oracle-checkpoint rescoring, and a four-way LongNav failure-type taxonomy.

setting.backbone: Frozen commercial MLLM APIs: GPT-5.6-Luna, GPT-5.5, GPT-5.4, GPT-5.2, Claude-Opus-5, Claude-Opus-4.6, Gemini-3.8-Flash, Gemini-3.6-Flash, Gemini-3.1-Pro, Doubao-Seed-2.0-Pro, GLM-5V-Turbo, Kimi-K3
setting.training_data: none (training-free evaluation of off-the-shelf MLLMs; benchmark only)
setting.observation: first-person RGB from a simulated character, text interaction history and an optional bounded frame buffer, plus an interactive georeferenced overhead map with no route
setting.action_space: structured continuous-motion primitives (move/sprint with direction and duration up to 2 s, look yaw/pitch, jump) plus map actions and terminate, at most 150 steps
setting.simulator: Unity-based UrbanGround (Hong Kong 3D Tiles + 3D Pedestrian Network)
setting.privileged: none (no coordinates, distance-remaining, shortest path or route API exposed to the model)

numbers.extra: 150-step limit; 810 base instances; no official split, so the whole benchmark is reported as test

numbers_note: Custom benchmark without official splits, so 'test' is used as a placeholder. Only the best or representative models are listed; the paper reports 12 models in Tables 1-4 and in Appendix Tables. Figures give distance-bin success and partial-progress values without exact numbers.
results: Models do well on local recognition (best 93.8%) and short navigation (best 81.3%), but orientation is weak (best 58.3%) and long navigation is near zero (best 5.0%). Road-closure and pedestrian tasks are almost never solved (SR at most 3.8%), even though pedestrian-network adherence stays around 93-98%; closure compliance is at most 46.7% and pedestrian-collision rates are 76.3-90.0%.
limitations: Evaluation only, with no method to improve agents, and a single city (Hong Kong) with only 810 base instances, so per-subtask cells are small (e.g. 60-80 items).
Only frozen commercial MLLMs with a text-history ReAct protocol are evaluated, with no memory modules, agent frameworks, or fine-tuned models, so failures may partly reflect the prompting protocol.
Navigation success is coarse (15 m radius, binary), with no SPL or NE, and no quantitative human baseline is reported beyond feasibility.
